reason: Re-opened packet.js tanakh 104 --verse 21.1 and found the evidence words verbatim in Radak on 21:1, so the words exist and verse.js and entry-check both pass. Two attacks land. PLAIN: 'seven sons of Saul are hanged' says more than the text. day.js 21:8 names them as the two sons of Rizpah whom she bore unto Saul and the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul whom she bore to Adriel: five are his daughter's sons, his grandsons (Radak himself on the chapter says they were Merab's sons, raised by Michal). The text's own phrase is 'seven men of his sons' (21:6); the clause flattens it into seven sons of Saul, a factual misstatement in a hard passage. ATTRIBUTION: the reading is not Radak's. His comment on ויבקש דוד את פני ה' is a relay of two others' answers: first Saadia Gaon's (first year he thought it chance, second the sin of Micah's idol, third he knew it was another sin), closed with אלה השאלות והתשובות כך סידרם רבינו סעדיה גאון, then ומה שפירשו רבותינו ז"ל, the Talmudic year-by-year search (Yevamot 78b). He endorses neither. 'Radak ... reads the three years as' puts under his name the second of two reported readings, and passes over the one he gives first and at length; 'citing the sages' discloses the source but the verb still makes it his reading. By the standard, a reading he merely transmits alongside a rival does not stand as his.
better: Plain: 'seven of Saul’s sons and grandsons are hanged at the Gibeonites’ demand'. Reading: Metzudat David on 21:1 (lemma ואל בית הדמים) gives his own account: Saul’s house is called bloody because he shed blood and Israel did not protest; the blood is the Gibeonites killed with the priests of Nob, where they served as hewers of wood and drawers of water for the house of the LORD; Israel could not protest the priests’ killing because Saul said they had rebelled and conspired with David. Words: ועל מה שהיו בית שאול בית הדמים, כי דם שפך, ולא מיחו בו ישראל ... כי כשהרג כהני נוב הרג אז גם הגבעונים. If Radak is kept, the reading must say he sets Saadia Gaon’s answer beside the sages’ without choosing.
